sourcedFrom: OPERATOR'S MANUAL — USP SERIES — Covering USP, USP Compact, and USP Specialized Models — June 2026 (imprint page) (2026)
cleanIntro: A hammer-fired 9x19 service pistol on a modified Browning-type linkless action, 4.25 inch cold-hammer-forged polygonal barrel, 10- or 15-round magazines. The frame-mounted control lever — safety, decocker, or both, depending on which of ten variants you own — is the control that makes a USP a USP, and the field strip runs through the slide release axle rather than any takedown lever. HK's USP SERIES book covers the full-size USP, the USP Compact and the Specialized models in one volume, so start by finding your gun in it.

steps.title: One book, three families, ten variants — find YOUR USP9 first
steps.action: Confirm the model and the variant before trusting any control description. The cover scopes this book to the USP, USP Compact and USP Specialized models; the Section 3 table prints USP9 as its first model row — 9mm x 19, 10 & 15 round magazines, 4.25 inch barrel. Then identify the trigger variant, because the control lever's function (safety, decocker, both, or absent entirely on Variant 7 and LEM guns) depends on which parts are installed, and the function check at the end of this strip is printed per-variant.
steps.prose: The USP is a modular design and HK sells the same pistol in ten trigger/firing-mode configurations. Every clearing and stripping step below is common to all of them, but what the lever above your thumb does is not — and assuming a decock function that is not there is how hammers get lowered by hand on live chambers.
steps.quote: The USP is available in both full-size frame, compact models, as well as specialized models, with ten trigger/firing mode configurations and three calibers—.45 ACP, .40 S&W, 9mm (special order on some models).
steps.cite: OPERATOR'S MANUAL — USP SERIES — Covering USP, USP Compact, and USP Specialized Models — June 2026 (imprint page) — Section 1 — INTRODUCTION, p.6

steps.title: Treat it as ready to fire until magazine out AND chamber checked
steps.action: Muzzle in a safe direction, finger off the trigger and outside the guard. Your USP9 may have no conventional manual safety at all, so nothing about the levers tells you it is safe — only removing the magazine and confirming the chamber by eye and by finger does.
steps.prose: HK puts this sentence on the cover page before the table of contents, because a USP without the SAFE-position lever looks identical at a glance to one with it.
steps.quote: Like most modern handguns, the HK USP pistol may be equipped in a configuration that does not have a conventional manual safety. Therefore, you must consider it to be loaded and ready to fire until you have removed the magazine and visually and physically (with your finger) confirmed that the chamber is empty.
steps.cite: OPERATOR'S MANUAL — USP SERIES — Covering USP, USP Compact, and USP Specialized Models — June 2026 (imprint page) — Cover page
steps.warn: Most USP variants will fire with the magazine removed if a round is chambered — only special models with a magazine disconnect are the exception.

steps.title: Magazine out — hand under it, paddle catch, out
steps.action: Hold your support hand under the magazine, press the paddle magazine catch at the rear of the trigger guard, and take the magazine out of the well. The USP uses a paddle you press down with the trigger finger or thumb, not a push button — if you find yourself hunting for a button on the grip, you are on the wrong control.
steps.prose: The magazine comes out first, before the slide moves. Rack first and the slide helpfully feeds a fresh round out of the magazine you meant to remove.
steps.quote: 2. Remove the magazine. 1. Hold your hand under the magazine. 2. Press paddle magazine catch (Fig. 9-A) 3. Remove magazine (Fig. 10-B).
steps.cite: OPERATOR'S MANUAL — USP SERIES — Covering USP, USP Compact, and USP Specialized Models — June 2026 (imprint page) — Section 5 — CLEARING AND SAFETY CHECK PROCEDURE, p.25

steps.title: Slide locked back, watching the port as it opens
steps.action: Grasp the rear serrations and rack the slide fully rearward with the muzzle still safe, push up on the slide release, and let the slide ease forward until it locks on the release. Watch the ejection port while you do it — a chambered cartridge or an empty case should come flying out, and seeing what left the gun is part of the check.
steps.prose: The USP locks open off the left-hand slide release; pushing and holding it up as the slide comes back is the coordination this step asks for.
steps.quote: 3. Open and lock the slide to the rear. Grasping the rear serrations, rack the slide to the rear while keeping the muzzle pointed in a safe direction (A). Push and hold upwards on the slide release (B) and lock the slide to the rear by allowing the slide to move forward until it engages the slide release. Watch for a cartridge or empty case to be ejected out through the ejection port.
steps.cite: OPERATOR'S MANUAL — USP SERIES — Covering USP, USP Compact, and USP Specialized Models — June 2026 (imprint page) — Section 5 — CLEARING AND SAFETY CHECK PROCEDURE, p.25

steps.title: Chamber checked by eye AND by finger — then the feed ramp
steps.action: With the slide locked open, look into the chamber through the ejection port, then physically insert a finger through the port and sweep the chamber and feed ramp area. Remove anything you find. If a cartridge stays put, run the whole clearing procedure again; if it will not extract, stop and take the pistol to a gunsmith rather than prying at it.
steps.prose: HK's order is deliberate: the visual check finds most rounds, the finger sweep finds the one sitting in shadow on the feed ramp that the eye missed.
steps.caution: Never pry at a stuck cartridge with a metal tool — a primer strike from a screwdriver ruptures cases.
steps.quote: 4. Inspect the chamber. Inspect the chamber for the presence of a cartridge or empty case by: 1. Visually inspecting the chamber through the open ejection port. 2. Physically inserting a finger through the ejection port and sweeping the chamber and feed ramp area. 3. Removing any cartridges or empty cases from the chamber or from within the USP. 4. If the cartridge remains in the chamber, repeat the Clearing Procedure. If the cartridge will not extract, contact a gunsmith.
steps.cite: OPERATOR'S MANUAL — USP SERIES — Covering USP, USP Compact, and USP Specialized Models — June 2026 (imprint page) — Section 5 — CLEARING AND SAFETY CHECK PROCEDURE, p.25

steps.title: Slide forward, thumb over the frame, find the retention tab
steps.action: Depress the slide release and let the slide run forward off the lock. Now hold the pistol so your thumb covers the rear of the frame and your fingers rest on top of the slide, and with the firing hand pull the slide back to the position where the retention tab of the slide release shows through the recess on the left side of the slide. Hold it exactly there.
steps.prose: This is the fussiest moment of a USP strip: the slide has one position, about a half inch back, where the axle is free. Too far forward or too far back and the release will not budge — that resistance is the alignment telling you to adjust, not to push harder.
steps.quote: 4. Using the firing hand, pull the slide back to the rear so that the retention tab of the slide release is visible through the recess on the left side of the slide (see Fig. 13).
steps.cite: OPERATOR'S MANUAL — USP SERIES — Covering USP, USP Compact, and USP Specialized Models — June 2026 (imprint page) — Section 6 — DISASSEMBLY, p.27

steps.title: Push the slide release axle out from the right, remove it left
steps.action: With the non-firing hand, press on the axle of the slide release from the RIGHT side of the frame and remove the slide release completely out of the left side. It is a firm push with a thumb — no punch needed on a maintained pistol — and the lever comes away as one piece. Set it where it cannot roll.
steps.prose: Unlike a 1911's slide stop this lever does not want to be wiggled free at an angle; it presses straight through. If it fights you, re-check the slide position from the last step before applying force.
steps.quote: 5. With the non-firing hand, press on the axle of the slide release from the right side of the frame, and completely remove the slide release from the left side of the frame.
steps.cite: OPERATOR'S MANUAL — USP SERIES — Covering USP, USP Compact, and USP Specialized Models — June 2026 (imprint page) — Section 6 — DISASSEMBLY, p.27

steps.title: Slide group forward and off — control the recoil assembly
steps.action: Slide the whole upper — slide, barrel and recoil spring assembly — forward off the frame rails and set the frame aside. Keep a hand under the recoil assembly as the slide comes free: it is held under spring tension, and uncontrolled it can launch, hurt you, or disappear under the bench.
steps.prose: The frame is now inert plastic and steel inserts; everything under tension left with the slide. That is why the order is axle first, slide second.
steps.quote: 6. Remove the slide with barr­el and recoil spring assembly by slidi­ng it forward off of the frame (see Figure 14).
steps.cite: OPERATOR'S MANUAL — USP SERIES — Covering USP, USP Compact, and USP Specialized Models — June 2026 (imprint page) — Section 6 — DISASSEMBLY, p.27
steps.warn: The recoil assembly is under spring tension until it is deliberately released in the next step.

steps.title: Recoil spring assembly out — forward, up, and to the side
steps.action: Turn the slide upside down and carefully push the captive recoil spring assembly forward, then up and out to either the left or right side, separating it from the barrel and slide. The USP's assembly is captive — spring, guide rod and the recoil-reduction buffer are one unit — and HK says leave it that way: do not take the assembly itself apart.
steps.prose: The recoil reduction system that lets the USP digest +P is inside this assembly, and it needs no adjustment and no internal cleaning — which is exactly why disassembling it is discouraged.
steps.caution: The captive recoil spring assembly is removed as a unit and never taken apart.
steps.quote:
7. Turn the slide upside down and carefully push the recoil spring forward, up, and out
to either the left or right side, separating the recoil spring from the barrel and slide (see Figure 15). The USP series pistols use a “captive” recoil spring assembly, disa­ s­sem­bly is not recommended.
steps.cite: OPERATOR'S MANUAL — USP SERIES — Covering USP, USP Compact, and USP Specialized Models — June 2026 (imprint page) — Section 6 — DISASSEMBLY, p.28

steps.title: Barrel out through the ejection port
steps.action: Pivot the barrel slightly forward and press upward on it through the ejection port; the locking block lifts out of engagement and the barrel comes free of the slide. Four groups on the bench: slide, barrel, recoil spring assembly, frame.
steps.prose: The lug you are pressing on is the barrel locking block — the same surface that locks into the ejection port in battery. Pressing anywhere else just wedges the barrel in the slide.
steps.quote: 8. Pivot the barrel slightly forward and press upward on the barrel through the ejection port, separating the barrel from the slide.
steps.cite: OPERATOR'S MANUAL — USP SERIES — Covering USP, USP Compact, and USP Specialized Models — June 2026 (imprint page) — Section 6 — DISASSEMBLY, p.28

steps.title: ⛔ Bronze brush only — the bore is polygonal
steps.action: Clean the bore with a bronze bristle brush and solvent, at least six passes chamber to muzzle, then patches until clean. Never a steel brush: the USP9's bore is polygonal, and steel bristles scratch the polygon and cost accuracy that does not come back.
steps.prose: This is HK's one barrel-specific cleaning rule and it exists because of how they make barrels — there are no sharp lands to protect, just a hardened polygon whose surface finish is the accuracy.
steps.quote: Do not use a steel bore brush which can scratch the polygonal bore and reduce accuracy.
steps.cite: OPERATOR'S MANUAL — USP SERIES — Covering USP, USP Compact, and USP Specialized Models — June 2026 (imprint page) — Section 8 — CLEANING & MAINTENANCE, p.41

steps.title: Field strip complete — everything further is armorer territory
steps.action: The user strip ends at these four groups. HK's own line under the last disassembly figure is that only a certified armorer goes further — the control lever internals, sear and hammer group are not owner-serviceable, and on the USP specifically HK flags that 2005-era hammer and catch parts must never be mixed across revisions. Clean at the intervals the book gives: Normal after each firing or every twelve months, Major after 600 cartridges or exposure to sand, dust or water.
steps.prose: The USP's modularity is real — variants convert by installing different parts — but the book is explicit that conversion parts and anything behind the frame rails belong to HK-trained hands.
steps.quote: Disassembly of the pistol is now comp­ lete. Only an HK certified armorer should disassemble the pistol further.
steps.cite: OPERATOR'S MANUAL — USP SERIES — Covering USP, USP Compact, and USP Specialized Models — June 2026 (imprint page) — Section 6 — DISASSEMBLY, p.28

deepSteps.title: ⛔ Ammunition bounds: no +P+, no steel or aluminum case, no reloads
deepSteps.action: Feed the USP9 quality brass-cased factory ammunition to NATO, SAAMI or CIP spec and nothing else. The book bars +P+ outright, along with reloaded, remanufactured, steel-cased, aluminum-cased and handloaded ammunition — and separately bars military surplus, corrosive-primed, cast lead, and submachine-gun-loaded cartridges. The recoil reduction system is rated for +P; +P+ is a different thing with no defined pressure standard.
deepSteps.prose: On a polygonal bore, cast lead is not a taste question — it plates the polygon and raises pressure. And the +P/+P+ line is exactly where HK draws it, so read headstamps, not marketing.
deepSteps.quote: USP pistols are designed to fire quality, brass-cased, factory-loaded ammunition loaded to NATO, SAAMI (Sporting Arms and Ammunition Manufacturers’ Institute), or CIP (Permanent International Commission for the Proof of Small Arms) specifications for use, specifically in handguns. DO NOT USE “+P+”, reloaded, remanufactured, steel cased, aluminum cased, or handloaded ammunition because it may not meet applicable NATO, SAAMI or CIP standards and could cause death, serious personal injury, and/or damage to your pistol and may void your warranty.
deepSteps.cite: OPERATOR'S MANUAL — USP SERIES — Covering USP, USP Compact, and USP Specialized Models — June 2026 (imprint page) — Section 5 — AMMUNITION, p.17

deepSteps.title: ⛔ Never lower the hammer by hand on a loaded chamber
deepSteps.action: If your variant has a decock function, decock with the lever — that is what it is for. Manually lowering the hammer with the trigger pulled takes the hammer past the half-cock notch and bypasses every passive safety in the pistol; on DA/SA models without the decocking function HK states flatly that lowering the hammer on a loaded chamber is unsafe.
deepSteps.prose: The printed procedure for Variant 9/10 hammer-lowering exists only for an EMPTY chamber, and it is three warnings deep for a reason. If the lever on your gun decocks, use it; if it does not, the hammer stays where the action put it.
deepSteps.quote: On DA/SA models without the decocking funct­ion in the control lever, it is unsafe to lower the hammer while there is a round in the chamber.
deepSteps.cite: OPERATOR'S MANUAL — USP SERIES — Covering USP, USP Compact, and USP Specialized Models — June 2026 (imprint page) — Section 5 — LOADING, p.19
deepSteps.warn: Manual hammer-lowering bypasses the passive safeties. Decock with the lever or not at all.

deepSteps.title: Magazine floorplate off — high-capacity pattern
deepSteps.action: For the 15-round magazine: depress the locking detent in the floorplate with a blunt pointed instrument and hold it, put a hand over the base to control the spring, then slide the floorplate forward off the housing. Let the locking plate and spring expand out gradually, then lift out locking plate, spring and follower. The 10-round magazine adds a second catch: with the detent depressed you also squeeze the locking tabs on both sides of the magazine before the parts release.
deepSteps.prose: The two magazine patterns strip differently and the book gives each its own numbered procedure — check which you are holding before pushing on anything spring-loaded.
deepSteps.quote: 4. Gradually allow the lock­ing plate and magazine spring to expand out of the magazine housing.
deepSteps.cite: OPERATOR'S MANUAL — USP SERIES — Covering USP, USP Compact, and USP Specialized Models — June 2026 (imprint page) — Section 6 — MAGAZINE DISASSEMBLY, p.35
deepSteps.warn: Keep the base of the magazine pointed away from your face and eyes — the spring is fully compressed against the floorplate.

deepSteps.title: Major cleaning at 600 rounds — magazines apart, everything immersed
deepSteps.action: Major cleaning is normal cleaning plus two escalations: the magazine comes apart for cleaning, and all parts are rinsed with or immersed in cleaning solution and scrubbed with a nylon brush, then dried with compressed air or rag and swabs. The trigger is a 600-cartridge count, or any exposure to sand, dust or water — saltwater especially.
deepSteps.prose: Dry everything completely before lubricating and reassembling; solvent trapped in the firing pin channel is how light strikes get invented.
deepSteps.caution: Ultrasonic cleaning can strip the colored reference markings off the frame, extractor and control lever, and is normally unnecessary.
deepSteps.quote: Major Cleaning - Major Cleaning is the same as normal cleaning except that: • The magazine is disassembled for cleaning, following the instructions in Section 6. • All parts should be rinsed with or immersed in cleaning solution and thoroughly scrubbed with a nylon brush. The parts can be dried using compressed air or with a rag and cotton swabs.
deepSteps.cite: OPERATOR'S MANUAL — USP SERIES — Covering USP, USP Compact, and USP Specialized Models — June 2026 (imprint page) — Section 8 — Major Cleaning, p.43

deepSteps.title: ⛔ Do not alter parts — and never mix old and new hammer/catch parts
deepSteps.action: HK bars altering any part of the pistol or magazine — 'improving' it included — on pain of injury, damage and a voided warranty. The USP carries one extra, model-specific trap: the catch was revised in 2005 to fit a revised hammer, and mismatching old and new hammer/catch parts creates a genuine safety issue. Any work in that group is armorer work, with part numbers verified before installation.
deepSteps.prose: Both units look nearly identical installed, which is exactly why the book prints photographs of them side by side and asks for part-number verification rather than eyeballing.
deepSteps.quote: In 2005, the USP catch was modified to fit the revised USP hammer. Both of the units pictured below function in the same manner if installed properly. However, a safety issue is created if the parts are mismatched. Please verify that the part numbers and the correct assembly are completed before installation. Improper installation or mismatched parts can result in a severe malfunction.
deepSteps.cite: OPERATOR'S MANUAL — USP SERIES — Covering USP, USP Compact, and USP Specialized Models — June 2026 (imprint page) — Section 9 — HAMMER AND CATCH NOTIFICATION, p.45

deepSteps.title: Lock-Out Device: the key lock in the grip, and the LEM catch
deepSteps.action: USPs made after October 1999 carry HK's internal Lock-Out Device in the lanyard-loop insert: two-pronged key, quarter turn clockwise to lock, and the action — trigger, hammer and slide — is frozen. Holes horizontal means locked. On LEM-equipped pistols there is a sequence: the pistol must be cleared and dry fired once to release the compressed hammer spring before the lock will engage.
deepSteps.prose: The lock also freezes the slide closed — forcing the slide on a locked pistol damages it. If the slide will not move and you did not expect that, check the lock before diagnosing anything else.
deepSteps.caution: When the Lock-Out Device is locked, the slide is locked closed — do not force it.
deepSteps.quote: In USP pistols fitted with the Law Enforcement Modification (LEM), the pistol must first be unloaded, “CLEARED”, and dry fired to release the compressed hammer spring before the Lock-Out Device can be locked.
deepSteps.cite: OPERATOR'S MANUAL — USP SERIES — Covering USP, USP Compact, and USP Specialized Models — June 2026 (imprint page) — Section 10 — LOCK-OUT DEVICE, p.46

cleaning.name: SLIDE
tasks: Gently scrub all internal surfaces with a nylon toothbrush moistened with cleaning solution
Remove all loose fouling with a rag and cotton swabs

cleaning.name: BARREL AND LOCKING BLOCK
tasks: Bronze bore brush with cleaning solution, at least six passes chamber to muzzle — NEVER steel on the polygonal bore
Scrub the barrel exterior and locking block with the nylon toothbrush, then wipe with rag and swabs

cleaning.name: RECOIL SPRING ASSEMBLY AND FRAME
tasks: Remove all visible fouling from the captive recoil spring assembly — solution, nylon toothbrush, rag and swabs; never disassemble it
Scrub the frame where carbon shows, concentrating on the area normally covered by the slide and the unlock block area that meets the barrel

cleaning.name: MAGAZINE
tasks: Scrub the top of the magazine — follower and feed lips — with the nylon toothbrush
Disassemble the magazine only at Major cleaning
After reassembly confirm the follower runs freely and rises nearly flush to the feed lips

cleaning.name: INTERVALS AND LUBRICATION
tasks: Normal cleaning after each firing or every twelve months, whichever comes first
Major cleaning after 600 cartridges, or after sand, dust or water — saltwater especially

Light lube on the barrel exterior and all metal parts; medium lube on the barrel locking block, slide rails and grooves, interior controls, extractor and sear; nothing on plastic, rubber or ammunition

reassembly: Position the barrel in the slide: muzzle in the front hole, locking block in the ejection port, the angled locking surfaces visible along the bottom of the slide.
Install the recoil spring assembly so the front of the guide rod engages the small hole in the front of the slide.

Align the opposing angled locking surfaces on the rear of the guide rod with those on the bottom of the barrel locking block, then push the assembly forward until the recoil spring retainer engages the shelf on the front of the locking block.
Hold the slide with a thumb keeping the rear of the recoil assembly seated, and check the sear axle does not protrude from either side of the frame.
Position the rear of the slide above the front edge of the frame and slowly draw it back, pressing down on the disconnector so the frame's metal inserts pick up the slide grooves.
Retract the slide until the left-side recess sits over the slide release axle hole, hold it, and insert the slide release from left to right until flush.
Clear the pistol, confirm the slide runs freely, then run the function check for YOUR variant — the book prints five different checks (V1/2, V3/4, V5/6, V7, LEM).
fncheck: Clear the USP9 again and rack the slide three or four times in quick succession — it must run without binding. Then run the printed function check for your variant, not a generic one: on a V1/V2 the hammer must not fall on SAFE, must fall single-action on FIRE, must be caught by the sear with a metallic click when the slide is cycled with the trigger held, and must fire double-action from the decocked state; on a V7 or LEM there is no control lever and the check is the double-action cycle and trigger reset. Finish by confirming the slide locks back on an inserted empty magazine.
